examples.text: Костя, мы сейчас домой едем или как?
examples.trans: Kostya, are we going home right now or what?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'there is'.

examples.text: Может быть, вы нам что-нибудь споёте?
examples.trans: Maybe you will sing something for us?

examples.text: У меня есть машинка.
examples.trans: I have a toy car.

examples.text: Детство было трудное.
examples.trans: Childhood was hard.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'a minute (diminutive)' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Скажите, у вас сейчас есть минутка?
examples.trans: Tell me, do you have a minute right now?

examples.text: Дай на минутку.
examples.trans: Let me have it for a minute.

examples.text: Есть минутка?
examples.trans: Have you got a minute?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Да, конечно, у нас это суперзвезда.
examples.trans: Yes, of course, she is a superstar here.

examples.text: Конечно, подменю тебя, не переживай.
examples.trans: Of course, I will cover for you, do not worry.

examples.text: Конечно, какой приятный запах на кухне!
examples.trans: Of course, what a pleasant smell in the kitchen!

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ятный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('nice, pleasant').

examples.text: Конечно, какой приятный запах на кухне!
examples.trans: Of course, what a pleasant smell in the kitchen!

examples.text: Приятного аппетита!
examples.trans: Enjoy your meal!

examples.text: Он очень приятный человек.
examples.trans: He's a very nice person.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'aroma, smell' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Конечно, какой приятный запах на кухне!
examples.trans: Of course, what a pleasant smell in the kitchen!

examples.text: Запомни, у нас двести второй номер.
examples.trans: Remember, we have room two hundred and two.

examples.text: Собака нашла запах плохой травы!
examples.trans: The dog found the smell of bad herbs!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, я внимательно слушаю, Элеонора Андреевна.
examples.trans: Yes, I am listening attentively, Eleonora Andreyevna.

examples.text: Миша, скоро у нас модный показ.
examples.trans: Misha, soon we will have a fashion show.

examples.text: Нам нужно очень хорошо к нему подготовиться.
examples.trans: We need to prepare very well for it.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.text: Конечно, какой приятный запах на кухне!
examples.trans: Of course, what a pleasant smell in the kitchen!

examples.text: У неё такой домашний кухонный фитнес.
examples.trans: She has that kind of home kitchen fitness.

examples.text: Мы сидим на кухне.
examples.trans: We're sitting in the kitchen.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'look', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.text: Можно я посмотрю?
examples.trans: May I have a look?

examples.text: Я только посмотрел.
examples.trans: I only had a look.

examples.text: А можно я пойду посмотрю?
examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Посмотрите туда, это ваша известная певица?
examples.trans: Look over there, is that your famous singer?

examples.text: Тебе туда плохое мясо положили.
examples.trans: They put bad meat in there for you.

examples.text: Пойдём туда вместе.
examples.trans: Let's go there together.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'вестный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('famous, well-known').

examples.text: Сейчас это самый известный модный модельер.
examples.trans: Right now he is the most famous fashion designer.

examples.text: Она у нас очень известная певица.
examples.trans: She is a very famous singer in our country.

examples.text: Слушай, ты знаешь такую известную певицу?
examples.trans: Listen, do you know such a famous singer?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'singer' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Да, её зовут певица Елена.
examples.trans: Yes, her name is the singer Elena.

examples.text: Она у нас очень известная певица.
examples.trans: She is a very famous singer in our country.

examples.text: Слушай, ты знаешь такую известную певицу?
examples.trans: Listen, do you know such a famous singer?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да, я внимательно слушаю, Элеонора Андреевна.
examples.trans: Yes, I am listening attentively, Eleonora Andreyevna.

examples.text: Нет, милая, я никуда не смотрел.
examples.trans: No, darling, I was not looking anywhere.

examples.text: Ну давай купим у него что-нибудь.
examples.trans: Well let us buy something from him.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Костя, мы сейчас домой едем или как?
examples.trans: Kostya, are we going home right now or what?

examples.text: Ты поезжай домой, а я останусь здесь.
examples.trans: You go on home, and I will stay here.

examples.text: Не волнуйся, утром сразу приеду домой.
examples.trans: Do not worry, in the morning I will come straight home.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').

examples.text: Да, это моя любимая будущая жена.
examples.trans: Yes, that is my beloved future wife.

examples.text: Вот это любимое платье моей Елены.
examples.trans: Here is my Elena's favorite dress.

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('future, next').

examples.text: Моя будущая жена ваша большая поклонница.
examples.trans: My future wife is a big admirer of yours.

examples.text: Да, это моя любимая будущая жена.
examples.trans: Yes, that is my beloved future wife.

examples.text: Значит, это ваша будущая жена?
examples.trans: So this is your future wife?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Моя будущая жена ваша большая поклонница.
examples.trans: My future wife is a big admirer of yours.

examples.text: Моя жена хотела дать большой концерт.
examples.trans: My wife wanted to give a big concert.

examples.text: Подождите, ваша жена большая знаменитость?
examples.trans: Wait, is your wife a big celebrity?
